mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce corporate investments and consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS > 5% and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS increases > 1% MoM, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5%, or if the correlation between a sharp rise in UNRATE and negative 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) declines by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals a contraction in supply-side activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to concerns about economic slowdown and reduced corporate output.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines > 1% MoM, or if the correlation between INDPRO decline and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a low and stable CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicates controlled inflation, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it reduces uncertainty and supports consumer purchasing power.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL is stable, or if the correlation between stable CPIAUCSL and positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) and Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) signals robust demand and labor market strength, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and PAYEMS both increase > 1% MoM
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when both HOUST and PAYEMS increase > 1% MoM, or if the joint correlation between these increases and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) during an economic expansion signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased costs for businesses.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE declines > 0.3% during economic expansion, or if the correlation between falling UNRATE and negative 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a combination of rising Industrial Production (INDPRO) and falling Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) signals strong supply-side growth and labor market tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises > 1% MoM and UNRATE falls > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO rises and UNRATE falls as specified, or if the joint correlation between these conditions and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
